title: Debug: Part 2
summary: Trace mutation, aliases, boundaries, and multi-step state.
refresher: Deeper Python bugs often begin before the failing line. Track **object** identity when data is shared, inspect types beside **values**, and test empty, one-item, and boundary inputs.

sections.title: Check whether two names share one object
sections.summary: Mutation bugs often come from two **variables** pointing at the same **list**.

blocks.body: In Python, assignment gives another name to the same object. That is harmless for numbers and **strings** because they do not mutate in place. **Lists** and **dictionaries** are different: if two names point at one list, changing the list through either name changes the same object.

blocks.title: Find the first wrong state
blocks.caption: Compare the expected state with the actual state before the final answer distracts you.

steps.title: Before the update
steps.body: The total is still correct before this loop pass.

steps.title: Wrong update
steps.body: The update changes the wrong variable or uses the wrong operation.

steps.title: Fix the transition
steps.body: Once the first bad transition is known, the fix is smaller.

blocks.caption: The first version prints `[1, 2, 3]` because both names reach the same **list**. The second version **leaves** `original` as `[1, 2]`.
Printing `id` is useful when you need to confirm whether two **variables** name the same **object**.
blocks.code:
a = [1]
b = a
c = a.copy()
print(id(a) == id(b))
print(id(a) == id(c))

blocks.prompt: What does `b = a` do when `a` is a **list**?
choices: converts the list to a tuple
blocks.why: Both names refer to one **list** **object**, so later list mutations are visible through both names.

sections.title: Test the smallest inputs on purpose
sections.summary: Empty and one-item inputs expose assumptions hidden by normal examples.

blocks.body: A bug can hide when every example has several items. Before trusting a **loop**, try the smallest inputs: an empty **list**, a one-item list, and a list where the answer appears at the first or last position.

blocks.caption: Negative indexing is still indexing. `items[-1]` works only when the **list** has at least one element.

blocks.why: An empty **list** has no last element, so the code needs a branch before using `items[-1]`.

sections.title: Print values with their types
sections.summary: A wrong type can make a correct-looking line behave differently.

blocks.body: When arithmetic or comparisons look strange, print the value and its type together. A string that looks like a number is still text until you convert it.

blocks.caption: The type name explains why the comparison or addition may not behave the way you expected.
blocks.code:
value = "12"
print(value, type(value).__name__)
number = int(value)
print(number + 3)

choices: To confirm what kind of value the code really has
To change every value into an integer
blocks.why: Seeing the type beside the value can reveal text-number mixups and other wrong assumptions.

sections.title: Find the first wrong state
sections.summary: Debugging gets easier when you stop at the first bad transition.

blocks.caption: **Print** the value before and after the update so you can see exactly which pass changes the state incorrectly.
blocks.code:
total = 0
for score in scores:
    print("before", score, total)
    total += score
    print("after", score, total)

blocks.title: Debug: Part 2 checklist
items: Check whether two names share one **object**.
Log **values** with their types when arithmetic or comparisons look odd.
Find the first line where the state changes incorrectly.

sections.title: Choose copy, mutate, or build new data
sections.summary: List and dictionary bugs get easier once you choose how data should change.

blocks.body: Before changing a collection, decide whether the original should change. If yes, mutate it deliberately. If no, make a copy or build a new result.

blocks.caption: Building a filtered result avoids index shifts while removing items.

blocks.prompt: Why can building a new list be safer than removing while looping?
choices: The scan does not fight shifting indexes
It skips the empty case automatically
blocks.why: Removing from the same list being scanned can shift later items into positions the loop has already passed.

debug-p2-01.title: Empty input changes the math
debug-p2-01.body: A formula that works for normal data can fail when the collection has no items.
debug-p2-01.notice: Check the divisor or first access before running the normal-case calculation.
debug-p2-01.mistake: Do not divide by a count before checking whether the count is zero.

debug-p2-02.title: Reset per-row state inside the outer loop
debug-p2-02.body: State for one row should restart before scanning that row.
debug-p2-02.notice: Ask whether the variable belongs to the whole grid or only the current row.
debug-p2-02.mistake: Do not let a previous row leak into the next row's total.

debug-p2-03.title: Binary search moves toward the possible half
debug-p2-03.body: When the middle value is too small, the target must be to the right in sorted data.
debug-p2-03.notice: Move the lower bound past mid when mid is too small.
debug-p2-03.mistake: Do not move a boundary backward into the half you already ruled out.

debug-p2-04.title: Removal shifts later items
debug-p2-04.body: Removing the current item moves the next item into the same index.
debug-p2-04.notice: After removal, either recheck the current index, move backward, or build a filtered result.
debug-p2-04.mistake: Do not increment blindly after a removal if adjacent items may also need removal.

debug-p2-05.title: Initial best must come from possible data
debug-p2-05.body: A starting best value that is not in the input can beat every real value by accident.
debug-p2-05.notice: For maximum or minimum, initialize from the first item when possible.
debug-p2-05.mistake: Do not use zero as a default when all real values might be below zero.

debug-p2-06.title: Second place may need distinctness
debug-p2-06.body: Tracking largest and second largest requires a rule for duplicates.
debug-p2-06.notice: Decide whether equal-to-largest values are allowed before updating second.
debug-p2-06.mistake: Do not let the same value occupy both largest and second when the prompt asks for distinct values.

debug-p2-07.title: Do not count the first value twice
debug-p2-07.body: Preloading a running total and then looping over every item can add the first item again.
debug-p2-07.notice: Choose either start at zero and loop all items, or start at first and loop the rest.
debug-p2-07.mistake: Do not combine both patterns unless the prompt needs double counting.

debug-p2-08.title: Mirror checks need opposite sides
debug-p2-08.body: A palindrome-style comparison pairs the left position with the matching right position.
debug-p2-08.notice: Compute the right index from the length and the left index.
debug-p2-08.mistake: Do not compare neighboring characters when the prompt asks for mirrored characters.
